stages.name: No war elephants
stages.desc: Lands that neither kept nor fought with war elephants

stages.name: Carthaginian elephant country
stages.desc: Carthage's hunting grounds, stables and elephant bases

stages.name: Numidian & Mauretanian lands
stages.desc: African kingdoms that caught elephants and supplied them to others

stages.name: Elephants at war
stages.desc: Lands where war elephants marched and fought

stages.name: Roman-controlled
stages.desc: Under Rome's rule or firm control

states.name: France
timeline: Gallic peoples; the Greek colony of Massalia on the coast
Hannibal's elephants cross the Rhône on rafts and head for the Alps
The elephants have passed into Italy

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Mauretania: the Atlas forests, the most lasting home of the North African elephant
King Baga of Mauretania escorts Massinissa home with four thousand horsemen

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberian and Celtiberian peoples; Carthaginian trading posts such as Gades
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades; Carthage's elephants come to Spain
Hannibal leaves; Rome lands in Spain and Hasdrubal's elephants fight on
After Ilipa, Carthage loses Spain; Rome holds the east and south
At Numantia, Rome's Numidian elephants panic and rout their own army
The Celtiberian war ends in a truce

states.name: Libya
timeline: Greek Cyrenaica under the Ptolemies; Carthage holds the Emporia coast of the Syrtes
Massinissa seizes lands of the Emporia from Carthage; Rome does not intervene

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage's homeland; its walls are later said to have stabled three hundred elephants
Regulus invades Africa; at Adys the elephants are trapped on wooded hills
After the Bagradas victory, Carthage rebuilds its elephant corps
The Mercenary War: Hamilcar's and Hanno's elephants fight the rebels
The revolt is crushed; the elephant herds are rebuilt
Scipio lands near Utica; Zama is fought in 202
By the peace, Carthage surrenders its elephants and may train no more
Rome declares war; the three-year siege of Carthage begins
Carthage is destroyed; its lands become the Roman province of Africa

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome holds the peninsula; in Sicily, Carthage's elephants fight at Agrigentum
Carthage gives up Sicily, Rome's first province
Hannibal's elephants cross the Alps and fight at the Trebia
Hannibal is recalled to Africa; Rome holds Italy again

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Numidian kingdoms of the Masaesyli and Massylii, in elephant country of the Tell and Atlas
Massinissa of the Massylii changes sides and allies with Rome
Syphax is captured; Massinissa rules all Numidia from Cirta
Massinissa's elephants serve Roman armies abroad, as far as Spain

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Lusitanian peoples of the Atlantic west
Viriathus leads the Lusitanians against Rome

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Ptolemaic Egypt: its kings hunt African elephants far to the south, along the Red Sea
At Raphia, Ptolemy IV's African elephants flee from Antiochus's Indian ones

states.name: Malta
timeline: A Carthaginian island and naval station
The Roman consul Sempronius takes Malta

events.title: Siege of Agrigentum
events.text: Hanno brings some fifty to sixty elephants to relieve the city; the Romans defeat him and sack Agrigentum.

events.title: Regulus lands
events.text: A Roman army under Marcus Atilius Regulus lands at Aspis, east of Carthage.

events.title: Battle of Adys
events.text: Regulus beats a Carthaginian army camped on wooded hills, where its elephants are useless.

events.title: Bagradas battle
events.text: The Spartan Xanthippus leads nearly a hundred elephants on open ground and destroys Regulus's army.

events.title: Shipwreck off Camarina
events.text: The fleet rescuing the Roman survivors is wrecked by a storm off Sicily.

events.title: Battle of Panormus
events.text: Metellus's javelin-men in a trench drive the elephants back into their own army.

events.title: Elephants in Rome
events.text: Over a hundred captured elephants are rafted to Rome and shown in the Circus.

events.title: Battle of Drepana
events.text: Carthage wins its one great sea victory of the war.

events.title: Aegates Islands
events.text: Rome's new fleet wins the war; Carthage gives up Sicily.

events.title: Hanno at Utica
events.text: Hanno's hundred elephants storm the rebel camp at Utica, but he loses the victory.

events.title: Battle of the Macar
events.text: Hamilcar Barca, with seventy elephants, defeats the mercenaries by the Bagradas river.

events.title: The Saw
events.text: Hamilcar traps the mercenary army in a defile and destroys it.

events.title: Hamilcar in Spain
events.text: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades to build a new Carthaginian dominion in Spain.

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal, Hamilcar's son-in-law, founds Carthago Nova as the Barcid capital.

events.title: Battle of the Tagus
events.text: Hannibal's forty elephants trample an Iberian army crossing the river.

events.title: Siege of Saguntum
events.text: Hannibal besieges Rome's ally Saguntum, and the Second Punic War begins.

events.title: Rome takes Malta
events.text: The consul Sempronius Longus seizes Malta from its Carthaginian garrison.

events.title: Scipio at Emporion
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio lands in north-eastern Spain to fight the Carthaginians there.

events.title: Crossing the Rhône
events.text: Thirty-seven elephants are ferried over the Rhône on earth-covered rafts.

events.title: Crossing the Alps
events.text: Elephants, horses and men struggle over a high pass in the autumn snow.

events.title: Battle of the Trebia
events.text: The elephants help break the Roman army in December; most die of cold soon after.

events.title: The last elephant
events.text: Hannibal rides the only surviving elephant through the flooded Arno marshes and loses an eye.

events.title: Battle of Raphia
events.text: Ptolemy IV's African elephants recoil from the larger Indian elephants of Antiochus III.

events.title: Battle of Cannae
events.text: Hannibal destroys a Roman army, without a single elephant.

events.title: Elephants at Locri
events.text: Bomilcar lands reinforcements and elephants for Hannibal at Locri.

events.title: Battle of Dertosa
events.text: The Scipio brothers defeat Hasdrubal Barca and his elephants on the Ebro.

events.title: Elephants at Capua
events.text: Hannibal's elephants attack the Roman siege lines around Capua.

events.title: Battle of Baecula
events.text: Scipio defeats Hasdrubal Barca, who escapes north towards Italy.

events.title: Battle of the Metaurus
events.text: Hasdrubal's elephants run wild; their riders kill them with mallet and chisel.

events.title: Battle of Ilipa
events.text: Scipio routs Hasdrubal Gisco's thirty-two elephants and wins Spain.

events.title: Baga's escort
events.text: The Mauretanian king Baga sends four thousand horsemen to escort Massinissa home.

events.title: Massinissa takes Cirta
events.text: Syphax is captured and Massinissa becomes king of Numidia.

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.text: Hannibal's eighty elephants fail against Scipio's open lanes and trumpets.

events.title: The elephant ban
events.text: The peace forces Carthage to hand over all its elephants and train no more.

events.title: Hannibal flees
events.text: Accused by Rome, Hannibal escapes from Carthage to the east.

events.title: Emporia seized
events.text: Massinissa seizes the rich Emporia coast from Carthage.

events.title: Panic at Numantia
events.text: A Numidian elephant struck by a stone panics the others, and the Romans flee.

events.title: War with Massinissa
events.text: Carthage raises an army against Massinissa, breaking the treaty of 201.

events.title: Siege of Carthage
events.text: Rome declares war and lays siege to Carthage.

events.title: Massinissa dies
events.text: The Numidian king dies at about ninety; his kingdom is divided among his sons.

events.title: Viriathus
events.text: The Lusitanian leader Viriathus begins his war against Rome.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Scipio Aemilianus storms and burns Carthage; survivors are sold into slavery.

chartNote: Share of the mapped area, by each present-day country's role in the story of the war elephant. Regions are today's boundaries, which cut across ancient peoples and kingdoms; the map is a simplification, and vast desert countries such as Algeria, Libya and Egypt swing the shares. Roman control of Spain and northern Italy was far from complete in this period.
